title: Fireball — illustrative behavior profile
description: A deliberately small, transparent example used to teach the distinction between an authored behavior model and its paper and digital adapters. It is not a validated Physics provider or a canonical spell rule.

model.energyContinuing: max(0, energyAtTarget - deliveredEnergy) + max(0, deliveredEnergy - targetResistance) * passThrough

impactBands.label: Negligible
impactBands.description: A trace, flare, or momentary disturbance.

impactBands.label: Light
impactBands.description: Noticeable but limited harm or disruption.

impactBands.label: Moderate
impactBands.description: Meaningful harm; the target or scene is changed.

impactBands.label: Heavy
impactBands.description: Severe harm or substantial structural/environmental effect.

impactBands.label: Devastating
impactBands.description: Overwhelming local effect; consequences extend beyond the immediate target.

paperAdapter.note: The target number is selected by comparing the workshop-sampled probability of reaching the meaningful-effect threshold with the 2d6 distribution. The harm bands are a compact human-readable projection of the same samples.

examples.label: Miss — energy carries on
examples.narrative: The casting line misses the intended target. Most of the energy continues into the space beyond; the miss is not a declaration that the effect vanished.

examples.label: Hit — target takes the effect
examples.narrative: The target intersects the casting path. Resistance absorbs part of the delivered energy; the remainder produces a meaningful impact.

examples.label: Critical — exceptional alignment
examples.narrative: The casting conditions align unusually well. More energy reaches the target, less is lost to resistance, and the surrounding scene receives a stronger secondary effect.
